quick_brief: Week 1 Challenge: Test your skills in drawing coordinate geometry and the Turtle library, and storing and manipulating inputs in variables!

questions.text: What is the default library in Python that we use to draw lines and geometric shapes with interactive cards?
Which code do we use to declare and create a new turtle object to start drawing?
Which command directs the turtle to move forward 150 steps?
To change the direction of the turtle left at exactly a right angle, what angle should be written into the left function?
What is the basic function used to receive keyboard input and text interactively from the user?
When you write the code: steps = input("Enter space: "), what is the default data type for the variable steps?
Which conversion function do we use to convert written input texts into integers valid for comparison and mathematical operations?
What is the role of the t.color("blue") command when running turtle?
options: Change the background color of the entire screen
Change the color of the turtle's line and body to blue
Clear graphics and cleanse the interface
questions.correct: Change the color of the turtle's line and body to blue

questions.text: What throw command do we write at the end of the turtle script to keep the graphical window open and avoid its sudden closing?
What is the virtual coordinate space for the turtle to launch at the center of the drawing board?
Write the code to receive a text entry with the student's name and store it in a variable called 'student_name', then print a built-in greeting phrase 'Welcome, champion' followed by the name.
questions.correct_code:
student_name = input("Enter your name: ")
print("Welcome, hero" + student_name)

questions.text: Write the complete code in Python to configure the turtle, draw a straight line 120 steps long in green, then point it to the right at a 90 degree angle.
questions.correct_code:
import turtle
t = turtle.Turtle()
t.color("green")
t.forward(120)
t.right(90)
